title: 1959 AHSME Problem 22
statement: The line joining the midpoints of the diagonals of a trapezoid has length \(3.\) If the longer base is \(97,\) then the shorter base is:

solutions.text:
If the shorter base is \(b,\) the diagonal-midpoint segment has length half the difference of the bases: \[ \frac{97-b}{2}=3. \] Thus \(97-b=6\) and \(b=91.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Recall the length of the segment joining the diagonal midpoints of a trapezoid
It equals half the difference of the base lengths
